bibl.title: Gestational diabetes and pregnancy outcomes - a systematic review of the World Health Organization (WHO) and the International Association of Diabetes in Pregnancy Study Groups (IADPSG) diagnostic criteria

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: TWO COMPETING DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA FOR ONE CONDITION, COMPARED ON OUTCOMES - the WHO and IADPSG definitions of gestational diabetes, meta-analysed across eight cohorts and 44,829 untreated women
span.quote: The definition of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) as any degree of glucose intolerance with onset or first recognition during pregnancy is largely accepted. However, the precise level of glucose intolerance characterizing gestational diabetes has been controversial over the last three decades.

span.label: whether gestational diabetes as defined by the WHO criteria and as defined by the IADPSG criteria predicts adverse pregnancy outcomes, and whether the IADPSG criteria hold outside the study that generated them
span.quote: Because the HAPO study was used to generate the IADPSG criteria, we performed post hoc subgroup analysis excluding the HAPO study (Figure 7 ) for all outcomes for which it contributed data. For the analyses of the IADPSG criteria, the pooled RRs after exclusion were always somewhat smaller than the RR for the HAPO study alone. After exclusion, the pooled RRs remained statistically significant for preeclampsia (p = 0.006), but not for large for gestational age and cesarean delivery.

span.label: pooled relative risks for both criteria across five outcomes, with leave-one-out sensitivity analyses removing first the study that generated one set of criteria and then the study that supplied individual patient data
span.quote: For the three outcomes for which meta-analyses were possible for both criteria (large for gestational age, preeclampsia and cesarean delivery), the magnitude of the effects were similar for the WHO and the IADPSG criteria (1.53 vs. 1.73; 1.69 vs. 1.71; 1.37 vs. 1.23, respectively), although the inconsistency across studies limited aggregate estimation for the IADPSG criteria.

span.label: critique
span.quote: It is important to note that these crude associations are very small within a diagnostic context. Two reasons may explain the small associations found. First, both GDM criteria, especially the IADPSG criteria, identify lesser degrees of hyperglycemia when compared to other ones, such as those previously recommended by the ADA [ 20 ]. Second, as all the studies analyzed in this review excluded women receiving specific treatments for GDM (see Table 1 ), the range of hyperglycemia classified as GDM represents a mild degree of hyperglycemia.

span.label: a condition whose concept is agreed and whose boundary has been contested for thirty years
span.quote: The definition of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) as any degree of glucose intolerance with onset or first recognition during pregnancy is largely accepted. However, the precise level of glucose intolerance characterizing gestational diabetes has been controversial over the last three decades.

span.label: systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of cohort studies applying a 2 h 75 g OGTT universally, restricted to untreated women, with crude associations only
span.term: systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of cohort studies applying a 2 h 75 g OGTT universally, restricted to untreated women, with crude associations only
span.quote: As our aim was to investigate diagnostic criteria based on their capacity to predict GDM-related outcomes for classification purposes rather than for etiological investigation, all statistical analyses were crude, without adjustment for potential confounders.

span.label: THE CLEANEST SEPARATION IN THE CORPUS OF WHAT A THING IS FROM WHERE ITS LINE IS: `The definition of gestational diabetes mellitus as ANY DEGREE OF GLUCOSE INTOLERANCE WITH ONSET OR FIRST RECOGNITION DURING PREGNANCY IS LARGELY ACCEPTED. However, THE PRECISE LEVEL OF GLUCOSE INTOLERANCE CHARACTERIZING GESTATIONAL DIABETES HAS BEEN CONTROVERSIAL OVER THE LAST THREE DECADES.` The concept is settled and the threshold is not
span.quote: The definition of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) as any degree of glucose intolerance with onset or first recognition during pregnancy is largely accepted. However, the precise level of glucose intolerance characterizing gestational diabetes has been controversial over the last three decades.

span.label: AND ONE REASON THE CUT POINTS DIVERGED IS A UNIT-CONVERSION PROBLEM ACROSS ERAS: `different cutoffs for the diagnosis of GDM were chosen, ONE OF THE ISSUES BEING THE DIFFICULTY IN CONVERTING BLOOD GLUCOSE VALUES FROM THE ORIGINAL STUDIES DONE IN THE 1960s AND 1970s TO THEIR PLASMA EQUIVALENTS ANALYZED USING NEW ANALYTIC METHODS`. A threshold's history is a measurement-technology history
span.quote: The NDDG opted, in pregnancy, to maintain the 3 h 100 g OGTT test, largely used and evaluated in the USA. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) and many other medical associations around the world adopted over the years this 3 h 100 g OGTT test. In so doing, different cutoffs for the diagnosis of GDM were chosen, one of the issues being the difficulty in converting blood glucose values from the original studies done in the 1960s and 1970s [ 1 , 3 - 5 ] to their plasma equivalents analyzed using new analytic methods.

span.label: AND THE CIRCULARITY IS MEASURED WITH A LEAVE-ONE-OUT RATHER THAN ARGUED: `Because THE HAPO STUDY WAS USED TO GENERATE THE IADPSG CRITERIA, we performed post hoc subgroup analysis EXCLUDING THE HAPO STUDY ... After exclusion, the pooled RRs remained statistically significant for preeclampsia (p = 0.006), BUT NOT FOR LARGE FOR GESTATIONAL AGE AND CESAREAN DELIVERY.` Two of three outcomes lose significance once the generating study is removed
span.quote: Because the HAPO study was used to generate the IADPSG criteria, we performed post hoc subgroup analysis excluding the HAPO study (Figure 7 ) for all outcomes for which it contributed data. For the analyses of the IADPSG criteria, the pooled RRs after exclusion were always somewhat smaller than the RR for the HAPO study alone. After exclusion, the pooled RRs remained statistically significant for preeclampsia (p = 0.006), but not for large for gestational age and cesarean delivery.

span.label: and the expectation is stated plainly: `since the IADPSG criteria were DERIVED FROM THE HAPO STUDY, LOWER PERFORMANCE OF THESE CRITERIA IN NON-HAPO SETTINGS IS TO BE EXPECTED`
span.quote: Additionally, since the IADPSG criteria were derived from the HAPO study, lower performance of these criteria in non-HAPO settings is to be expected. For large for gestational age and for cesarean delivery, results remained inconsistent across studies after excluding HAPO, which makes questionable the estimates of pooled RRs generated for these outcomes (the pooled RRs found were lower and not statistically significant).

span.label: AND THE SAME CRITERION IDENTIFIES 24% OR 74% OF CASES DEPENDING ON THE CENTRE: `the fasting value identified OVER 70% of all cases ... while when these criteria were applied to the HAPO study as a whole, the fasting value identified ONLY ABOUT 50% ... as THIS RATE IN HAPO VARIED FROM 24% (THAILAND) TO 74% (BARBADOS), whether these differences resulted from INCOMPLETE FASTING or from other specific study or population particularity CANNOT BE CONCLUDED`
span.quote: In fact, the application of the IADPSG criteria in two published studies [ 13 , 22 ] and in the EBDG database showed that the fasting value identified over 70% of all cases of GDM so defined, while when these criteria were applied to the HAPO study as a whole, the fasting value identified only about 50% of cases. However, as this rate in HAPO varied from 24% (Thailand) to 74% (Barbados)[ 23 ], whether these differences resulted from incomplete fasting or from other specific study or population particularity cannot be concluded from current information.

span.label: AND A STRUCTURAL REASON WHY ONE DEFINITION IS LESS STABLE THAN THE OTHER: `the IADPSG criteria are MORE VULNERABLE TO HETEROGENEITY ACROSS DIFFERENT SETTINGS BECAUSE THEY ALLOW THAT DIAGNOSIS BE MADE ON THE BASIS OF ONLY ONE OUT OF THREE POSSIBLE MEASURES`. An OR-rule over three tests makes the class depend on which test a population happens to fail - the same shape as hoste2006's `the worst of either`, with the instability named
span.quote: One hypothesis is that the IADPSG criteria are more vulnerable to heterogeneity across different settings because they allow that diagnosis be made on the basis of only one out of three possible measures (fasting, 1 h and 2 h). Given population variability in terms of the probability of being positive by fasting and post load values, as well as in terms of the possibility of having incomplete fasting (drank coffee or tea with sugar; for example), more heterogeneity could be found for the IADPSG criteria.

span.label: THE OUTCOMES ARE DEFINED BY THE ORIGINAL AUTHORS, NOT BY THE REVIEW: perinatal outcomes are `macrosomia (AS DEFINED BY THE AUTHORS)` and maternal outcomes are taken `ACCORDING TO INDIVIDUAL STUDY DEFINITIONS`. A meta-analysis of definitions whose own outcome definitions vary between the studies pooled
span.quote: We decided to analyze, as perinatal outcomes, large for gestational age births and macrosomia (as defined by the authors), as well as perinatal mortality (fetal death and early neonatal death). Regarding maternal outcomes, we chose to analyze cesarean delivery and preeclampsia according to individual study definitions.

span.label: and the exception is printed rather than smoothed: macrosomia is `defined by authors as birth weight > 4000 g, EXCEPT ABERG et al`
span.quote: As seen in Figure 2 , a total of five studies allowed evaluation of the association between GDM diagnosed through WHO criteria and fetal macrosomia (defined by authors as birth weight > 4000 g, except Aberg et al [ 12 ]). The corresponding pooled relative risk (RR) was 1.81 (95%CI 1.47-2.22; p < 0.001), with very homogenous results across studies (I 2 = 0%).

span.label: AND THE CRITERIA PREDICT WITHOUT DISCRIMINATING: `these crude associations are VERY SMALL WITHIN A DIAGNOSTIC CONTEXT` and `EVEN IF GDM DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA WERE TO REACH RELATIVE RISKS CLOSE TO 3 ... the relative risks would STILL BE UNLIKELY TO REFLECT MAJOR DIAGNOSTIC DISCRIMINATION IN TERMS OF POST TEST PROBABILITIES`. A definition can be significantly associated with an outcome and still not sort the people in front of you
span.quote: Nevertheless, even if GDM diagnostic criteria were to reach relative risks close to 3 for these adverse outcomes in such settings, the relative risks would still be unlikely to reflect major diagnostic discrimination in terms of post test probabilities [ 21 ]. This fact suggests the importance of investigating the contribution to risk discrimination of other factors, besides glycaemia, for these outcomes.

span.label: and the analyses are deliberately crude, for a reason tied to what the criteria are FOR: `As our aim was to investigate diagnostic criteria based on THEIR CAPACITY TO PREDICT GDM-RELATED OUTCOMES FOR CLASSIFICATION PURPOSES RATHER THAN FOR ETIOLOGICAL INVESTIGATION, all statistical analyses were crude, without adjustment for potential confounders`
span.quote: As our aim was to investigate diagnostic criteria based on their capacity to predict GDM-related outcomes for classification purposes rather than for etiological investigation, all statistical analyses were crude, without adjustment for potential confounders.

span.label: AND ONLY ONE STUDY IN EIGHT BLINDED THE STAFF TO THE TEST RESULT: `Most of the studies (6/8) had adequate selection of participants, HALF of them presented adequate test standardization and reported losses to follow-up and ONLY ONE STUDY informed that MEDICAL STAFF WAS BLINDED TO OGTT RESULTS`
span.quote: Most of the studies (6/8) had adequate selection of participants, half of them presented adequate test standardization and reported losses to follow-up and only one study informed that medical staff was blinded to OGTT results.

span.label: `a fasting glucose >= 5.1 mmol/L (92 mg/dl), or a one hour result of >= 10.0 mmol/L (180 mg/dl), or a two hour result of >= 8.5 mmol/L (153 mg/dl)`, derived from HAPO and `BASED ON PREGNANCY OUTCOMES`
span.quote: More recently, the International Association of the Diabetes in Pregnancy Study Group (IADPSG), after extensive analyses of the Hyperglycemia and Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes (HAPO) study [ 7 ], recommended new diagnostic criteria for GDM [ 8 ] based on the 2 h 75 g OGTT: a fasting glucose ≥ 5.1 mmol/L (92 mg/dl), or a one hour result of ≥ 10.0 mmol/L (180 mg/dl), or a two hour result of ≥ 8.5 mmol/L (153 mg/dl).

span.label: `DEFINED BY AUTHORS AS BIRTH WEIGHT > 4000 g, EXCEPT ABERG et al`
span.quote: As seen in Figure 2 , a total of five studies allowed evaluation of the association between GDM diagnosed through WHO criteria and fetal macrosomia (defined by authors as birth weight > 4000 g, except Aberg et al [ 12 ]). The corresponding pooled relative risk (RR) was 1.81 (95%CI 1.47-2.22; p < 0.001), with very homogenous results across studies (I 2 = 0%).

span.label: 24-74 — the share of IADPSG-defined cases identified by the fasting value alone, across HAPO centres - Thailand to Barbados, one criterion
span.quote: In fact, the application of the IADPSG criteria in two published studies [ 13 , 22 ] and in the EBDG database showed that the fasting value identified over 70% of all cases of GDM so defined, while when these criteria were applied to the HAPO study as a whole, the fasting value identified only about 50% of cases. However, as this rate in HAPO varied from 24% (Thailand) to 74% (Barbados)[ 23 ], whether these differences resulted from incomplete fasting or from other specific study or population particularity cannot be concluded from current information.
